newsitem.title: USA: MCI ordered to stop advertising claim.
newsitem.headline: MCI ordered to stop advertising claim.

text.p: A federal judge Tuesday ordered MCI Communications Corp to stop claiming in advertising that its local toll rates are always lower than Ameritech Corp's, telecommunications companies said.
U.S. District Judge Joan Gottschall entered a preliminary injunction against the claims in a case resulting from an MCI advertising campaign in April, Ameritech said.
During the campaign, Ameritech said, MCI claimed its rates were "always" lower than Ameritech's for these calls when they were actually higher than Ameritech's 93 percent of the time.

An MCI spokeswoman said that while Gottschall did order a stop to the advertising claim, she also noted in her opinion that MCI's rates are, have been and probably are likely to be for some time in the future lower than Ameritech's.
Ameritech said in a statement that while MCI has since lowered its rates, Ameritech still offers lower prices through Ameritech CallPacks, flat rate calling plans available to Chicago-area customers.
